newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tax changes coming in S.African public sector.
newsitem.headline: Tax changes coming in S.African public sector.

text.p: South Africa's tax laws will be changed from March next year so that public and private sector retirement funds are treated equally, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Wednesday.
"This means that lump-sum payments from public sector funds will, for tax purposes, be dealt with on the same basis as those from private sector funds," she said in a speech to parliament.

"The increasingly common transfer of benefits from public sector pension funds to provident funds has clearly been taking place because of the ability, through such transfers, to be effectively tax free. "This practice is highly undesirable," Marcus said.
She said two-thirds of any amount transferred from a public sector pension fund to a public or private sector provident fund would become taxable on the date of transfer.
"We wish to also point out that interest credited through such instruments as deferred benefits and medical savings accounts is taxable in the hands of the member.
"Such medical schemes are being investigated to determine the appropriate tax treatment," Marcus said.
